ConventionCapabilityIdArg.docs: CLI-boundary mirror of `ConventionCapabilityId` for the read-only resolve argument (IN-05, IN-06, AC-09). Introduced as a sibling of `capability::CapabilityNameArg` rather than a change to it: that mirror wraps the `agent-profiles.json` lookup key and is shared with `capability exec`, so retyping it in place would carry the matching contract into a command that does not have one and change what values that command accepts. The mirror exists at all only because the validated usecase value cannot itself implement clap's parsing trait — the usual R9 boundary-mirror pattern — and it holds that validated value in a private field. Its `FromStr` delegates to `ConventionCapabilityId::try_new`, which is the enforcing site; this mirror adds no check of its own, so the invariant reaches the driver already established rather than re-decided anywhere along the way. It is declared in `conventions_resolve` beside the driver that consumes it rather than in `capability`, so the private field is reachable without widening its visibility.

ConventionResolveDriver.docs: Primary adapter for `conventions resolve` (IN-05, AC-06, AC-08). It renders from the returned `ConventionResolution` and holds no second representation, so display and machine output cannot disagree; only the resolver's error type can produce a failure outcome, which is what keeps the empty result on the success path here rather than by a rendering convention. Introduced as its own driver rather than a branch of the existing write-side conventions driver for two reasons: widening that driver would change the public constructor of the add / update-index / verify-index surface, which this track does not touch, and resolve is driven by its own application service, whose separation evidence is recorded on `ResolveConventionsQuery`.

ConventionResolveInput.docs: Typed input for the read-only `conventions resolve` command (IN-05, IN-06, AC-06, AC-09). The capability is held as the boundary mirror `ConventionCapabilityIdArg` rather than an argument string — the usual R9 serde/CLI-boundary mirror pattern, since the validated usecase type cannot itself implement clap's parsing trait. That mirror carries an already-validated `ConventionCapabilityId`, established by `ConventionCapabilityId::try_new` and by nothing on this side, so the driver has nothing left to re-validate. It is that mirror rather than the shared `CapabilityNameArg` because this command's argument is the query side of an exact-match comparison, and a mirror that trims would decide matches at the CLI boundary. Field order mirrors `cli::ConventionsCommand::Resolve` and `usecase::ResolveConventionsQuery` exactly; the CLI variant is the fixed point of that chain.

ConventionShippingCheckDriver.docs: Primary adapter for the non-shipping check (IN-11, AC-18). It maps the two verdict variants and the error type onto the process outcome and adds no rule of its own; because the verdict's violating variant carries the offending paths, the rendered failure necessarily names them rather than summarising a count. Introduced as its own driver rather than a second branch of `TemplateDriver` because widening that driver would change the public constructor of the export surface, and the check is driven by its own application service, whose separation evidence is recorded on `ConventionShippingCheckService`.

ConventionShippingCheckInput.docs: Typed input for the read-only non-shipping check (IN-11, AC-18). Both fields stay `PathBuf`: a tree root is the truly-opaque case R9 permits — a caller-chosen filesystem location with no invariant of its own — while the invariant that does matter, staying inside `knowledge/conventions/`, belongs to the document paths the inventory produces and is owned by `ConventionDocumentPath`. Field names and order mirror `cli::TemplateConventionShippingArgs` and `usecase::CheckConventionShippingQuery`.

ConventionsDriver.docs: Baseline-identical write-side conventions driver, unchanged by this track; declared so the composition root's existing wiring accessor still resolves to a declared primary adapter alongside the newly added read-only resolve accessor.

TemplateDriver.docs: Baseline-identical export driver, unchanged by this track; declared so the template composition root's existing `template_driver` accessor still resolves to a declared primary adapter alongside the newly added check accessor.
